title: Decompose loader pipeline: canonicalize weight formats, consolidate shard metadata, decouple tokenizer handshake
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: The current model ingest/loader code has accumulated multiple ad-hoc paths for checkpoint formats, per-model sharding metadata, and a tight tokenizer handshake that prevents streaming and incremental loads. This results in slower cold starts, duplication of format conversion code, and fragile integrations when adding new checkpoint layouts or quantized formats.

Goal: Rework the loader into clear stages: 1) canonicalize weights into a narrow in-memory representation or memory-mapped view, 2) unify and validate shard metadata so placement and KV-offsets are deterministic, 3) decouple tokenizer/schema handshake into an async contract allowing streaming loader progress and early KV cache priming. The result should reduce cold-start latency, simplify adding new checkpoint formats, and make tokenizer integration compatible with streaming generation.

Scope: - Implement a canonical weight adapter layer that normalizes incoming checkpoints (HuggingFace sharded, safetensors, legacy format). - Introduce a compact shard-metadata manifest format and a validation step used by runtime placement/allocator. - Refactor tokenizer integration: move tokenizer descriptor exchange to an independent async step (tokenizer handshake), with fallbacks to on-disk tokenizers when network unavailable. - Provide compatibility adapters for existing pipelines and a migration shim for on-disk cache entries.

Out of scope: full format conversion tooling for third-party formats (we will provide adapters, not a full conversion service).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Loader exposes a stable adapter interface and test vectors for at least HF sharded, safetensors, and legacy single-file checkpoints.
2) Cold-start model load latency reduced by >=15% on median for common 7B/13B models in our staging benchmark.
3) Tokenizer handshake is decoupled: streaming generation can start tokenization before full weights are loaded; validated with an e2e streaming test.
4) All existing downstream consumers (runtime, dedicated bootstrap, private deploy agent) pass integration smoke tests.
5) Migration shim applied and rollout plan documented; no customer downtime for hosted endpoints during rollout.
notes:
Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Loader+Decomposition+Design
Benchmark dashboard (staging): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/loader-cleanup/staging-benchmarks
Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1367
Related RFCs: loader-adapter-rfc-2025.md
PoC findings: canonicalizing to a minimal float16-mapped view reduced memory copies but required careful alignment for quantized shards. We plan memory-map-first then lazy-convert pages to host format for quantized checkpoints.
